CAFE_STAFF.situation: The customer is at the counter of the corner cafe.
facts: Coffee drinks can be hot or iced at the same price.
Sizes are small or large. Large is $1 more.
Milk can be regular or soy at no extra cost.
The restroom is at the back of the cafe.
The hotel is right across the main street: cross at the crosswalk outside the cafe door, turn left, and it is a few steps up on the corner.

HOTEL_STAFF.situation: The guest is at the front desk of the hotel lobby.
facts: Check-in is from 3 p.m. Check-out is by 11 a.m.
There is a reservation under the guest's name: a standard room for one night, already paid.
Their room is 305 on the third floor. The elevators are in the lobby.

POLICE_OFFICER.situation: The visitor is at the front desk of the small police station at the south end of the town's main street. A patrol car is parked right next to the station.
facts: The patrol car can drive to any building on the main street: the cafe, the hotel, the drugstore, the post office, the diner, the bank, the laundromat, the flower shop, the barber shop and the visitor's home.
If the visitor does not say where it happened, the patrol car drives once around the main street.

SHOP_STAFF.situation: The customer is at the counter of the small drugstore on the town's main street.
facts: Cash and cards are both accepted.

TAXI_DRIVER.situation: The passenger has just waved down the yellow taxi on the town's main street and is sitting in the back seat.
facts: The corner cafe and the hotel are on the main street, right across from each other.

TOWN_PASSERBY.situation: On the sidewalk of the town's main street on a sunny day. Ben is walking around the town between work meetings. He has just stopped the other person with a friendly remark about the nice weather. They have not met before.
facts: The other person lives in this town.
The corner cafe and the hotel are on the main street, right across from each other.
